messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: high-severity - toolcall parser errors for customer 'Lyra Health' in VPC dedicated pool lyra-prod-pool. Error rate spike 11:34 UTC. Paging eng-oncall.

maria lopez: seeing it, joining. lyra reported toolcall failures impacting 100% of requests to /tools/claimProcessor in prod VPC.

jon chen: I can take first touch. what's the observed error? samples?

maria lopez: logs show JSON parse errors from the toolcall payload -> parser rejects due to unexpected nested array in "claims.items" field. sending snip.

maria lopez: ```
ERROR: toolcall_parser: invalid schema: expected object at claims.items[0], got array
request_id=abcd-1234
model=redwood-chat-2
route=lyra-prod/claimProcessor
```

ravi singh: my quick read: payload shape changed upstream in customer's system per last deploy; parser schema is strict on our side. Could be schema drift. Any canary or recent model change?

sophie kim: no model rollouts in lyra pool in last 48h per deployment history. We did push a parser enforcement config change 36h ago on the dedicated pool (tightened JSON schema). Could be that.

jon chen: ok makes sense. Mitigation plan options: 1) temporarily relax schema enforcement on lyra-prod-pool, 2) add a compatibility shim to accept array or wrap as object, 3) ask Lyra to roll back upstream payload change. Which is fastest?

maria lopez: fastest is relax enforcement. We have an autoscaling-safe flag to disable strict validate_json on the pool config. Can flip with no restart.

ravi singh: agree. Doing that now for minimal customer impact. tagging @ops-handoff for change control.

ops-handoff: acknowledge. preflight: creating change ticket. Noting that relaxing validation may let malformed payloads through but keeps service up.

jon chen: executing command to patch pool config: ```sh
redwoodctl pool patch lyra-prod-pool --set validate_json=false --token $REDACTED
```

deploy-bot: pool lyra-prod-pool updated: validate_json=false (change id: ZT-4829). No rolling restart required.

maria lopez: can folks confirm error rate drop?

jon chen: tailing logs... looks like errors dropped from ~92% to ~3% over last 30s. still seeing occasional reject lines for legacy requests.

ravi singh: starting to triage exemplar requests for the array case. capturing 5 failing samples to propose a compat shim.

sophie kim: reaching out to Lyra support lead (cc: @lyra-support) to notify them of temporary relaxation and ask for a timeline to fix their payloads. Draft message: "We've relaxed strict parser enforcement in your dedicated pool to restore availability. Please coordinate a fix to send claims.items as an object per integration doc. We can help patch on client side."

maria lopez: great. Also scheduling an on-call handoff in 20m so next oncall is aware. tagging @ops-handoff for the postmortem and customer impact note.

ops-handoff: noted. customer impact: all API calls to /tools/claimProcessor returned 5xx for ~11 minutes before mitigation, estimated affected requests ~1.2k. SLA impact tailing.

jon chen: collecting root cause artifacts: parser rule id, pool config diff, sample payloads, timeline. I'll attach to incident ticket.

ravi singh: quick proposal for durable fix: add a small compatibility layer in the toolcall gateway that detects an array at claims.items and normalizes to { items: [...] } before parsing. Rolling out to lyra pool only as a targeted feature flag. Low risk and reversible.

maria lopez: +1. Devs can ship a targeted shim with feature flag. We should pair with Lyra to ensure it matches their shape.

sophie kim: Lyra replied: they pushed a change this morning that accidentally switched to sending arrays; they will revert within 4 hours and also accept normalization. They asked us to keep the pool relaxed until they confirm.

jon chen: ok keeping validate_json=false until Lyra confirms revert. I'll schedule the targeted shim today and gate behind a feature flag for lyra-prod-pool only.

ops-handoff: creating incident ticket INC-2024-2115 with summary and timeline. assigning postmortem to @maria lopez and @ravi singh.

maria lopez: handoff to next oncall @ops-handoff in 15m. Key context: 1) validate_json disabled on lyra-prod-pool, 2) errors dropped after change, 3) Lyra rolling back upstream change, 4) plan to add compatibility shim.

ops-handoff: acknowledged. I'll monitor until Lyra confirms and then coordinate enabling strict validation again.

jon chen: +1, leaving logs and diffs in INC-2024-2115. handing off now, cya. :wave:

maria lopez: thanks all. Filing quick customer impact summary for CSM: "Lyra experienced ~11m outage to claimProcessor in dedicated pool due to upstream payload shape change; mitigated by temporary schema relaxation; durable fix planned." :thumbsup:

ops-handoff: incident status -> mitigated. follow-ups: postmortem, compatibility shim rollout, conversation with Lyra to prevent repeat.
